title: Docker CLI basics
idea: The `docker` command-line interface (CLI) sends each command to the Docker daemon, which does the work. Most commands read as `docker <object> <action>`.
points: Short forms work too: `docker ps` is `docker container ls`.
Add `--help` to any command to see its usage and options.
Commands take an id or name to pick a target: `docker stop api`.

parts.label: Client
parts.note: Every command starts here. The client sends your request to the daemon.

parts.label: Object
parts.note: The kind of thing to manage. Others: `image`, `network` and `volume`.

parts.label: Action
parts.note: What to do with it. `ls` lists, `rm` removes, `inspect` shows details.

parts.label: Option
parts.note: Changes the action. `-a` is the short form. This one includes stopped containers.

code.caption: One pass through the everyday commands, using the Book Store API.

walk.text: List the commands. Add `--help` to one, such as `docker run --help`, for its options.
Build an image from the Dockerfile here and name it `bookstore-api`.
Start a container named `api` in the background. The next page covers these flags.
Print what the app in `api` has written to its output.
Stop the container, then remove it. `docker rm` refuses a running container unless you add `-f`.
List images. The image stays after its container is removed.

pitfalls: Name the container, not the image: `docker stop api`, not `docker stop bookstore-api`.
Use `docker rm` for containers and `docker rmi` for images; they are not interchangeable.
Use `docker rm -f` sparingly: it kills a running container with no chance to shut down.

quiz.q: Which command is just a short form of `docker container ls`?
quiz.why: `docker ps` is an alias of `docker container ls`. `docker images` is the short form of `docker image ls`, which lists images.

takeaway: Learn the pattern once, then `--help` answers the rest.
